card.name: Capital F starting a word
card.fires_on: The letter F (or FL) standing alone as the first piece of a word, usually capitalized at the start of a heading, sentence or all-caps word. It is often followed by a longer word that is split into pieces, such as Fungal, Folate, FOLD, focal or fucans.

modes.label: Heading or sentence start
modes.description: A capital F begins a section heading or sentence, split off from the rest of the word.
modes.example: Fungal Infections<< F>>ungal infections, especially oral and vaginal candid

modes.label: All-caps word
modes.description: F or FL begins an all-caps warning word such as FOLD or FLUID.
modes.example: HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA ON CEFOTETAN RELATIVE TO OTHER CEPHALOSPORINS OF AT LEAST 3<< F>>OLD. IF A PATIENT DEVELOPS

modes.label: Lowercase f inside terms
modes.description: A lowercase f starts a medical word such as foci or folic.
modes.example: studies for colony-forming units, (6) hemoglobin electrophoresis for A 2 and F hemoglobin, and (7) serum<< f>>olic acid and B 12 levels

card.writes: It pushes the model toward fill-type words, which looks like a side effect of the F letter rather than a useful output.
card.plain: It fires when a word starts with a lone letter F that is split from the rest of the word.
